A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Conditional Clifford-Steerable CNN work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE forecasting experiments, model-scaling results, equivariance measurements, and qualitative prediction errors in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting and equivariance results and adds baseline evaluations, a conditioning ablation, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The conditional convolution, equivariant kernel parameterization, mean-pooled conditioning, ResNet backbone, circular masking, and MW2 normalization are retained. Max-pooling and random conditioning appear as ablation variants; the proposed default method is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Navier–Stokes, shallow-water forecasting with SWE-1 and SWE-5 setups, three-dimensional Maxwell equations, and relativistic Maxwell equations. Appendix C retains the same datasets and task requirements. The new ablation and timing study use existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates Transolver on NS, MW3, and MW2, whereas v1 reports it only on SWE-1. CViT comparisons expand from SWE-5 to all four data-efficiency tasks. Tables 1 and 4 therefore substantially strengthen comparator coverage within existing experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds an N=64 NS evaluation point, a SWE-1 conditioning comparison at N=256, and a GPU timing protocol. The reported equivariance-error denominator changes from the magnitude of a sum to the sum of separate norms in Equation 18, although the reported errors remain identical; a rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a direct test of conditioning choices: none, mean pooling, max pooling, and a fixed random multivector. Appendix D.2 adds comparative inference timing to test conditioning overhead. These address central design and efficiency questions beyond v1's existing scaling, equivariance, and qualitative-error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The new inference-time averages remain point estimates rather than repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New comparisons place Transolver ahead of C-CSCNN on electrodynamics: MW3 at N=512 gives 3.99e-4 versus 4.51e-4, and MW2 at N=2048 gives 0.17034 versus 0.2519. New conditioning and timing results are also reported, including 54.30 ms for C-CSCNN versus 53.83 ms for CSCNN. SWE-5 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explicit Clifford-algebra defining relation and grade-dimension formula. The equivariance-error definition also changes mathematically through its denominator. The conditional-equivariance proofs, completeness conjecture, and Appendix A algebraic demonstrations otherwise retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the performance claim from consistently outperforming baseline methods to outperforming standard CSCNNs and matching state-of-the-art baselines. The title drops 'with Complete Kernel Basis.' The central contribution of input-conditioned equivariant kernels remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a locality-based explanation for differing fluid and electrodynamics rankings, discusses richer conditioning for scaling, and identifies unoptimized Clifford operations as a runtime bottleneck. It also expands applicability discussion and adds limitations concerning multivector field representations. The general completeness conjecture and masking limitations were already disclosed in v1.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the existing equivariance evaluation as single-layer testing on NS, specifies standard-normal sampling for the random-condition ablation, and documents single-A100 timing averaged over the test set. Appendix B's architecture, masking, normalization, optimizer, and training-hardware details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: New references support discussion of equivariance at scale, robotics, control, vision, and physics applications, plus ConvNeXt and Flash Clifford as future improvements. The principal positioning relative to steerable CNNs, Clifford networks, and implicit kernels remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, abstract, introductory framing, and experimental narrative; separates Clifford-algebra background into its own subsection; and expands the conclusion with limitations and an impact statement. The overall section sequence and most method and proof prose remain recognizable and unchanged.

P2.justification: The document switches from one to two columns. The data-efficiency plots are consolidated into a four-panel Figure 2 focused on C-CSCNN versus CSCNN, while broader comparisons appear in Tables 1 and 4. Ablation and timing tables are added, and equivariance results move from a table into prose. Existing rollout, masking, and residual images are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons resolve a material weakness in v1's empirical positioning: v2 evaluates stronger electrodynamics baselines and acknowledges Transolver's advantage. The conditioning ablation and measured overhead substantiate central design and efficiency arguments. These gains are substantial despite remaining reporting gaps, including the unexplained SWE-1 mean-pooling MSE difference between Table 1 (0.3137) and Table 3 (0.2982).
